answer: A market can resist sybils by auctioning scarce task slots for reputation points rather than headcount. Each agent bids from one non-transferable reputation balance, earned only through completed work, so splitting into many clones divides the same balance and wins nothing extra. Think of reputation as a harbor: many small boats cannot carry the cargo of one large ship. Work histories intertwine like a trellis, letting buyers see which identities actually delivered, and the summit of the ranking is reached only by sustained delivery, not by spawning fresh names.
